widget.instructions: Press Play to run the motion; scrub the time slider to inspect any instant.

stem: A runner jogs {{d1}} m east in {{t1}} s, then {{d2}} m west in {{t2}} s.
What is the runner's average velocity for the whole run (east positive)?

hints.text: What is the runner's net displacement?

speed-for-velocity.text: You used the total distance, which gives the average speed. Average velocity uses the displacement.

mean-of-velocities.text: The two legs take different times, so you can't just average their velocities. Use total displacement ÷ total time.

dimension-mismatch.text: Check the unit: the answer is a velocity.

workedSolution.text: Displacement: {{d1}} − {{d2}} = {{net}} m east. Total time: {{T}} s.
Average velocity = {{net}} ÷ {{T}} = {{ans}} m/s east (average speed would be {{speed}} m/s).

speed-for-velocity.front: Average velocity or average speed: which uses displacement?
speed-for-velocity.back: Average velocity = displacement ÷ time; average speed = path length ÷ time.

mean-of-velocities.front: Is average velocity the mean of the stage velocities?
mean-of-velocities.back: Only if the stages take equal times. In general, total displacement ÷ total time.

accessibility.altText: Two lanes: the runner's eastward leg and the westward return.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Use Play and the time slider; type your answer in the box.
